source.title_on_document: The Homogenizing Effect of Large Language Models on Human Expression and Thought

supplement.holds: The document mentions no supplement or online appendix. Pages 18-19 hold Outstanding Questions and a Glossary; pages 21-38 are references.

paper_design_summary: Narrative review (opinion/review article) that synthesizes work from linguistics, psychology, cognitive science, and computer science on how LLMs homogenize language, perspective, and reasoning. It runs no experiment, collects no data, and reports no search protocol, inclusion criteria, or pooled estimates. Its creativity content is one paragraph (p. 15) citing experiments on LLM-assisted ideation (Anderson, Shah, and Kreminski 2024; Doshi and Hauser 2024).

assignment.quote: We synthesize evidence across linguistics, psychology, cognitive science, and computer science to show how LLMs reflect and reinforce dominant styles while marginalizing alternative voices and reasoning strategies.

synthesis.inclusion: not_stated: narrative review with no stated search strategy or inclusion criteria; 136 numbered references (pp. 21-38).

company_involvement.description: Funded by the Air Force Office of Scientific Research (A9550-23-1-046); authors at the University of Southern California. No company involvement stated.

eligibility.reason: Narrative review with no human participants, no new data, and no pooled estimates (pp. 2-17). It belongs in the synthesis reference list only. Its ideation evidence (p. 15) cites refs [124] Anderson, Shah, and Kreminski (2024) and [125] Doshi and Hauser (2024), which are screened as separate papers.

one_line_finding: Narrative review arguing that LLMs homogenize human language, perspective, and reasoning; for creativity it cites experiments in which ChatGPT-assisted participants produced more, more elaborated ideas that were more semantically similar across participants (p. 15, refs [124, 125]); it reports no new data or pooled numbers.
open_questions: The PDF on file is arXiv 2508.01491v2 (5 Jan 2026); the journal version (Trends in Cognitive Sciences, DOI 10.1016/j.tics.2026.01.003) was not checked and may differ.
